title: HiBREW Espresso Machines Compared: H10A vs H13 vs H7A vs H7B
metaDescription: HiBREW espresso machine lineup compared: H10A (entry bundle with separate grinder), H13 (machine + G5 grinder bundle), H7A (dual boiler, built-in grinder), and H7B (commercial-grade, 58mm portafilter) — which tier fits your counter and your coffee habit.
author: ByteBuy Team

sections.content: Every current HiBREW espresso machine now ships with a grinder in some form — the no-grinder entry model (H10 Plus) and the budget built-in-grinder model (H7 Lite) have both been discontinued. What's left splits into two real questions: do you want a separate standalone grinder bundled in, or a grinder built into the machine body — and do you need home-kitchen output or commercial-grade volume. That's what actually separates these four, not the 20-bar pressure figure they all share.

items.label: H10A + G3 Grinder — What's Included
items.value: Entry-level semi-automatic machine bundled with a basic separate G3 grinder — two units, lowest price in the lineup

items.label: H13 + G5 Grinder — What's Included
items.value: Semi-automatic machine bundled with the better G5 grinder as a separate unit — same bundle concept as the H10A, higher-spec grinder

items.label: H7A — What's Included
items.value: 20 bar, dual boiler system, built-in grinder with 30 grind levels — brew and steam at the same time, one unit

items.label: H7B — What's Included
items.value: Commercial-grade build, 58mm portafilter, dual-heating system, built-in grinder with 30 size settings, touch screen — designed for cafés, hotels, restaurants

items.label: Pressure
items.value: 20 bar across all four — the shared baseline, not the differentiator

items.label: Grinder Placement
items.value: Separate bundled grinder (H10A, H13) vs. built-in grinder (H7A, H7B) — this, plus home vs. commercial scale, is the real split

pros: All four hit 20 bar pressure, which is the standard for proper espresso extraction — you're not downgrading pressure by buying the cheaper model
A separate bundled grinder (H10A, H13) is usually easier to upgrade or replace independently than a grinder built into the machine body
The H7A and H7B's built-in grinders save real counter space versus running a separate grinder next to the machine
The H7A's dual boiler means you can brew and steam milk simultaneously rather than waiting between steps — a real workflow upgrade, not a spec-sheet number
The H7B's 58mm portafilter and commercial-grade build are a genuine step up for anyone brewing high volume, not just a bigger price tag on the same machine
cons: A built-in grinder (H7A, H7B) is harder to service or upgrade later than a standalone grinder you can simply swap out
Semi-automatic machines still require you to dose, tamp, and time the shot yourself — none of these are push-button automatic
The H13's G5 grinder bundle costs noticeably more than the H10A's G3 bundle for a grinder upgrade, not a machine upgrade — worth checking if that trade-off matters to you
The H7B's commercial-grade price and footprint only make sense if you're actually brewing at café-level volume; for home use it's significant overkill

items.question: Which HiBREW espresso machine should I buy?
items.answer: For the lowest entry price with a grinder included, the H10A + G3 bundle covers both pieces at once. If you want a noticeably better grinder bundled in and don't mind the extra cost, step up to the H13 + G5. If counter space matters more than grinder flexibility, the H7A's built-in grinder and dual boiler cover brewing and steaming at the same time. If you're brewing at café or restaurant volume, the H7B's commercial-grade build and 58mm portafilter are the only one of the four actually built for that.

items.question: Is a separate bundled grinder better than a built-in one?
items.answer: Not strictly better — it's a different trade-off. A separate grinder (H10A, H13) is usually easier to service, upgrade, or replace on its own if it wears out or you want a different grind profile later. A built-in grinder (H7A, H7B) saves counter space and keeps everything in one footprint, but if it needs service you're often dealing with the whole machine rather than swapping a standalone unit.

items.question: Is a dual boiler espresso machine worth it over a single boiler?
items.answer: It comes down to whether you make milk drinks regularly. A dual boiler (H7A, H7B) lets you brew espresso and steam milk at the same time instead of waiting for the machine to switch between the two — a real time-saver when making multiple cappuccinos or lattes back to back. For straight espresso or occasional milk drinks, that extra capability matters less.

items.question: What does 20 bar pressure actually mean on an espresso machine?
items.answer: It's the pump's rated maximum pressure, and 20 bar is now standard across this class. The important detail is that proper espresso extraction happens around 9 bar at the group head — the higher pump rating is headroom for maintaining consistent pressure, not a sign that more pressure makes better coffee. All four HiBREW models share the same 20 bar rating, so it's not what separates them; grinder placement and build scale (home vs. commercial) are.

sections.content: The 20 bar pressure number is identical across all four — what you're actually choosing between is where the grinder lives (bundled separately vs. built in) and whether you need home-kitchen or commercial-grade output. H10A + G3 if you want the cheapest complete setup, H13 + G5 if you want a meaningfully better bundled grinder, H7A if you make milk drinks regularly and want everything in one unit, H7B if you're brewing at café volume and need the commercial-grade build. Pick based on your counter space and actual brewing volume, not the pressure figure every model shares.
